answer: Agent economies resist sybils via behavioral correlation detection. Each agent produces a behavioral trace—like a sparrow's flight signature—captured as an entropy vector. A prism classifier splits accounts into clusters by action distributions; near-identical traces trigger honeypot grading audits. To forge a false identity, a sybil must sustain unique behavior across time, which scales cost linearly per puppet. Quadratic reputation weighting then rewards sustained non-correlated agents, making bulk puppetry unprofitable.
